name: Greater Los Angeles
_comment_why: The plan's success criterion is the developer driving a route this app made and finding it better than the freeway. The developer is in Westwood. Human gate #1 is five real commutes and gate #2 is twenty more, and neither can happen against a graph 350 miles away - so this region exists to put the feedback loop where the person tuning the score actually is.
_comment_counties: Los Angeles County is the whole of the intent. The bbox clips slivers of Ventura (west of Leo Carrillo) and San Bernardino (east of the Angeles Crest county line); both are edge, neither is a reason to claim the county. Northern Orange County is NOT a sliver and is listed in _comment_bbox: the box reaches past eight of its cities. It is still not claimed here, because `counties` says what the region is FOR and nobody is being routed to Buena Park on purpose - but see the ratio note in _comment_counts.
_comment_bbox: Argued, not asserted, and deliberately SMALLER than sfbay's 2.07 x 2.07 so the fifteen-minute build promise holds: 1.15 x 0.75 degrees. West to -119.00 keeps PCH and the Malibu canyons whole through Leo Carrillo; cutting at -118.9 would sever Yerba Buena and Decker mid-canyon, and a road clipped in half scores as two short ones. East to -117.85 reaches the far end of Angeles Crest (CA-2), which climbs past -117.9 before dropping to Wrightwood. South to 33.70 takes in the whole Palos Verdes peninsula, whose loop is the coastal-suburban case. North to 34.45 clears the San Gabriel crest - Mt Wilson is 34.226, Angeles Crest tops out around 34.35 - so the mountain highway is not truncated at its best part. WHAT THE SOUTH-EAST CORNER ACTUALLY TAKES IN, corrected 2026-09-19 by [[T-0142]] after agent/rv-pr68 measured it against PR #68: northern Orange County, not a sliver of it. Anaheim (33.8366,-117.9143) and Santa Ana (33.7455,-117.8677) - the county seat - are inside this box, and so are Fullerton, Buena Park, Garden Grove, Westminster, Seal Beach and La Habra. The earlier sentence here said the box excluded Orange County outright, which was prose contradicting the numbers beside it. The BOX did not move and must not move casually: `counts_from` pins the recorded counts to the box they were measured over, so cutting the corner back means re-running the extract, and whether the owner's commute crosses -117.85 or 33.70 is a question for the human, not for an agent tidying a comment. One consequence to carry: `primary` at 8.51x sfbay is partly this OC arterial grid, which the T-0107 ratio argument did not acknowledge. What this deliberately EXCLUDES: Irvine and everything south and east of it, the Inland Empire and San Diego. They are a different market, not a bigger bbox, and each degree costs build time and graph size for roads nobody here will drive this month.
_comment_dem: 3DEP needs four tiles for this bbox: n34w118, n34w119, n35w118, n35w119. Derived from the bbox by dem.tiles_for_bbox, not typed by hand. None is ocean-only - n34w119 looks like it should be (Santa Monica Bay) but carries Palos Verdes and the Malibu coast, so unlike sfbay's n37w124 there is nothing to exclude. All four are now pinned by sha256 in inputs/manifest.yaml ([[T-0142]], retrieved 2026-09-19), and dem.tile_for resolves through dem.tiles_for_region('la') rather than the sfbay TILES constant - until that landed, every LA point had NO elevation and the terrain terms of the score were silently zero.
_comment_counts: Recorded from a real extract, not invented, and counts_from says WHICH extract - source PBF, its byte size, when the run finished, and the bbox it was cut with. The bbox matters most: sfbay's counts were once left describing a larger box after the box was corrected, and every class read 20-26% low on the next real run with nothing in the file to explain why. region.py now refuses a counts_from.bbox that disagrees with the region's own bbox, so that cannot recur silently.
